text.p: Construction firm Fujita Corp said on Monday that it had formed a restructuring plan covering the period to March 31, 2000 and that its major creditor bank Sakura Bank Ltd had said it would accept the plan.
A Fujita spokesman said that other banks, including Tokai Bank Ltd , were likely to accept the restructuring programme.

"Sakura Bank said it would accept our plan and Tokai said that it was considering accepting it. They will give us support so that we will not have difficulties raising funds for our operations," the spokesman said.
He said Fujita would continue its support to its group company Towa Real Estate Development Co Ltd.
Under the restructuring programme, debt-ridden Fujita would try to cut its debts by 157.4 billion yen to 480 billion yen by the end of March 2000, the spokesman said.
It would also cut its workforce by 560 workers to 4,900 employees during period through natural attrition, a halt of new recruitment and an early retirement programme, he said.
The company would also try to improve the profit margin of it construction projects to 10.1 percent in 1999/2000 from 8.9 percent in 1996/97, he said.

Fujita aims to post a parent current profit of 10.4 billion yen on sales of 744 billion yen in fiscal 1999/2000, against an actual parent current profit of 8.16 billion on sales of 709.76 billion yen last fiscal year, he said.
